rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Same direction: R = P + Q
Opposite direction: R = |P − Q|

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Opposite vectors do not give R = P + Q.  ·  The direction after a subtraction belongs to the larger magnitude.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Draw the positive direction before attaching a sign.  ·  The parallelogram law reduces to these two lines when the vectors are collinear.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Vectors are added by the head-to-tail rule. Place the tail of the second vector on the head of the first. The resultant runs from the tail of the first to the head of the second.  ·  When two vectors point the same way along one line, the triangle collapses into a longer line. The magnitude of the resultant is R = P + Q, and the direction is that common direction.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: A zero resultant does not mean the vectors were never there.  ·  Scalars add without a direction check. Vectors do not.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: When they point in opposite directions, the head-to-tail path folds back. The magnitude is R = |P − Q|, and the resultant points in the direction of the vector with the larger magnitude.  ·  The general parallelogram result R = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ cosθ) contains both cases. θ = 0° gives cosθ = 1 and R = P + Q. θ = 180° gives cosθ = −1 and R = |P − Q|.  ·  A negative sign on a one-dimensional vector means the opposite direction. Subtracting is the same operation as adding the opposite vector.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Zero resultant  ·  The resultant points with the larger vector.  ·  Addition of Vectors — Same and Opposite Directions is based on fundamental principles.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The resultant of two equal opposite vectors is zero. The body they act on is then in translational equilibrium if no other force is present.
